thread:
Ashley: Heads-up — after last night's rollout (rollout: kernel-select-v2) we're seeing p99 tail blips under high conc. p95 looks fine but p99 jumps ~80-120ms when concurrency > 100. Could be KV eviction interplay. Anyone digging in? :thinking:
Mike: I saw the same in job perf/stage-2026-03-10. KV miss rate jumps from 4% -> 22% when concurrent reqs cross ~110. Throughput stable but tail latency moves. Perf ID: perf-9832.
Sara: throwing numbers from a quick run:
```
microbatch | conc | p95(ms) | p99(ms) | kv_miss_rate
8          | 60   | 48      | 78      | 5%
8          | 120  | 54      | 210     | 21%
16         | 60   | 44      | 70      | 4%
16         | 120  | 50      | 180     | 19%
32         | 120  | 58      | 260     | 27%
```
Looks like bigger microbatches help p95 a bit but p99 still vulnerable as kv_miss_rate climbs.
Dave: I pulled a flamegraph and kernel dispatch histogram for perf-9832. When a request misses the KV cache we route to the 'cold-kernel' path which has a different fused attention kernel and adds ~90ms. Under high conc the probability of hitting cold-kernel spikes due to eviction storms. Also saw kernel_queue_depth oscillations.
Mike: trace link: https://perf.internal/trace/perf-9832 — snippet from logs: `KV lookup miss, eviction=true, evict_set=hot-evict-7, fallback_kernel=cold-fused-v1` repeated ~3-7x per second during spikes.
perf-bot: ALERT: SLI breach detected on eng-runtime / p99 > 200ms for 5m (alert_id: sli-2026-03-10-7). Paging: @Ashley @Mike
Ashley: OK — likely root is eviction-induced kernel switching under concurrency. Two mitigations to try in parallel: 1) soften microbatch gating so we avoid rapidly shrinking batches during short bursts; 2) increase sticky TTL for hot KV entries (reduce eviction churn).
Sara: I'll run a simulation sweep across microbatch {8,16,32} and TTL {30s, 120s, 300s} using loadgen `tools/load_sweep.sh --conc 20..140` and capture kv_miss_rate + kernel_switch_rate. Command: `./tools/load_sweep.sh --profile perf-9832-sweep --mb 8,16,32 --ttl 30,120,300`
Dave: quick note — there's a regression in recent commit 0f4c9b2 (kernel-select heuristics) that reduced the hysteresis window for kernel routing from 200ms -> 40ms. That makes the runtime flip kernels faster when latency varies, which amplifies tail effects on eviction. Might revert or increase to 300ms.
Mike: I'll attach perf counters and cache stats after Sara's run. Also can add a temporary kernel sticky flag to avoid switching for requests that hit eviction events.
Ashley: Nice. Action items: Sara run sweep and post CSV + traces (due EOD), Mike gather perf counters and test sticky flag, Dave prepare a PR to bump hysteresis or gate by eviction-rate. I'll coordinate canary rollout if results look good. :thumbsup:
Sara: On it. Starting sweep now. Will post summary and top traces when done.
Ashley: Thanks — keeping this thread for follow-ups, will close after canary.
